name: Champaign-Urbana, IL
author: NerdieSanders
description:
**Champaign-Urbana** is a college town of ~216,000 in central Illinois — Champaign County plus Savoy, Mahomet, Rantoul, Tolono, St. Joseph, and Monticello.

The transit problem here is the inverse of a big metro's: demand is not spread across competing centers but collapsed onto a single corridor. The **University of Illinois** generates roughly a quarter of every trip on the map — its 60,848 students are **28% of the mapped population**, against about 5% for Chicagoland or Springfield. Downtown Champaign, Campustown, the Urbana medical district and downtown Urbana sit in a nearly straight 5 km line, with the outlying towns hanging off it.

High-quality demand from U.S. Census **LODES 2023**, with special demand for **Willard Airport** and **Illinois Terminal** — now the second-busiest Amtrak station in Illinois, at 236,153 passengers in FY2024 — **2 universities** (Illinois and Parkland College), and **12 employment, retail and heritage destinations** (Carle Foundation Hospital, OSF Sacred Heart, Market Place, the UI Research Park, Memorial Stadium, the State Farm Center, the Krannert Center, and the Allerton estate).

All **16 magnet coordinates were verified individually** rather than estimated — two published coordinates proved wrong by 1.2 km and 740 m and were corrected before the build. Event venues are weighted at annualized daily rates rather than peak attendance, so a stadium used seven days a year does not outweigh a hospital used every day.

Per-building **foundation-depth collision**, **free building in and under the Sangamon River and Lake of the Woods**, and college campuses rendered in game.
data_source: U.S. Census LEHD LODES (2023) origin-destination data; Overture / OpenStreetMap buildings; OpenMapTiles.
